svg.title: Launch speed follows the distance to the tag
svg.desc: Step chart of the pollen launcher target in RPM against the distance from the camera to the nearest hive tag in inches. Nearer than 110 inches the target is 2900 RPM. From 110 to 140 inches it climbs along a gentle curve in 2-inch steps, from 2900 to 3294 RPM, each step adding a little more than the last. From 140 inches on it is 3325 RPM. The 110 and 140 inch shots were measured on the robot; the curve between them is the formula RPM equals 2900 plus 425 times the fraction of the way from 110 to 140 inches raised to the power 1.1. A smooth yellow curve under the steps shows the formula itself. The RPM axis is stretched toward the top, not linear, so the gentle bend is visible: a farther shot needs more speed, and each step out adds a little more than the last.
svg.text: Launch speed follows the distance to the tag
Pollen launcher target from the Limelight's distance to the nearest hive tag: a curve through the two measured
shots, in 2-inch steps. In TeleOp it follows while the driver holds aim or launch; otherwise the speed holds.
Distance from the camera to the nearest hive tag (inches)
Pollen launcher target (RPM)
d = inches to the tag, rounded down to a 2-inch step.
Exponent 1 would be a straight line; 1.1 bends up a little:
the first step adds 22 RPM, the last adds 31.
farther needs more speed:
the formula is the smooth yellow curve,
the code runs it in 2-inch steps (green).
RPM axis stretched toward the top (not linear)
so the bend shows. Read values off the gridlines.
2900 at 110 in (measured), and nearer
140 in and beyond: 3325
3325 from 140 in (measured)
124 in: 3084 RPM, from the formula
The RPM axis is not linear: it is stretched toward the top so the gentle bend of the 1.1 exponent is visible. Every labeled
number is real. Settings in BotProperties: launchNearIn 110, launchNearRpm 2900, launchFarIn 140, launchFarRpm 3325,
launchCurve 1.1, launchBandIn 2. Tuning: a miss near the hive moves the near RPM, a miss far out the far RPM, a miss in
the middle moves the curve (up if the middle falls short). The operator's D-pad up / down trims the whole curve by 50 RPM.
